conventions: Preposition before a construct noun: the chapter applied rule 30's subtraction test uniformly and it divides four ways in this chapter. Fused, one unit headed on the construct noun — LIPHNE -> before (13.22), AL ODOT -> because of (13.24), BE + TAVEKH -> in (13.32, the suffix keeping its own it under rule 19). Split, each morpheme holding English of its own — AL PI -> according to / the commandment (13.3), AL YAD -> along by / the side (13.29). Do not mark the construct noun unrepresented to give the preposition the whole English; rule 22 reaches a repeated element, and a construct noun inside such a pair repeats nothing.

Disjunctive indirect questions (13.18, 13.19, 13.20): the particle that opens the question takes the ASV's whether, and the particle standing at the head of the second member takes its or, whether that particle is a second interrogative HE or an IM. Rule 17 names IM in that slot; this chapter writes HE there too, at 13.18 (he-chazaq hu ha-rapheh -> whether they are strong or weak), and it is read the same way. The explicit subject pronoun keeps only its own they or it, and the copula goes to the predicate adjective under rule 20.

Supplied English verbs: where a preposition stands whose own relation the ASV's supplied verb states, that verb — and any relative the recasting requires — joins the preposition's unit under rules 41 and 49, headed as rule 49 directs, on the English preposition where one remains and on the verb where none does: MIN -> who come of, headed on of (13.33), and LE -> to overcome, headed on overcome (13.30). Where no morpheme in the clause carries what the supplied verb states, it stays added under rule 20, with any subject supplied beside it: they brought in the asyndetic gapped clause at 13.23. Both readings are named in the units' own notes.
report: Checked all 41 candidate lemma groups. Every printed multi-treatment bucket is licensed by the source or by the English the ASV wrote: the waw takes So, Now, But, with, also and that as written (rule 14, open list); the article is unrepresented only where no 'the' stands before its own word (13.19 'what cities', 13.23 'a staff', 13.24 'That place' — rules 29, 41) and takes the second written 'the' wherever the rectum is rendered arthrously (13.16, 13.20, 13.26, 13.29, 13.32), while a single 'the' fronts onto the article before an anarthrous proper-name rectum (13.22, 13.28), which is rule 29's own division and not two analyses; the object marker takes English only where the ASV spends a word on the object relation (13.17 'into', 13.26 'unto' twice) and is bare elsewhere (rule 16); resumptive suffixes and HENNAH inside relative clauses go unrepresented (13.19, 13.32) while BAH and ALEHA fuse to 'therein' where the ASV writes that one word (13.18, 13.20), which is rule 22's fusion sentence.

Read the dump end to end for what the table cannot see, since it is keyed by source lemma and blind to added units. The chapter's three added units each answer to no morpheme: the appositional 'namely' between two juxtaposed LE-MATTEH phrases (13.11, rule 16's limit), the supplied clause verb and subject 'they brought' in an asyndetic gapped clause (13.23, rule 20), and the 'and' between two predicate adjectives the Hebrew joins with no waw (13.28, rules 14 and 42). Against these, 13.30 gives 'to overcome' to the LE and 13.33 gives 'who come of' to the MIN. That is not a split: in each of those a preposition stands whose own relation the supplied verb states, so rule 49's relational-verb subtraction applies, whereas 13.23's clause has no morpheme at all to carry a verb. Both are hedged in their own unit notes, and the heads follow rule 49 — 'of' where an English preposition remains, 'overcome' where none does.

One real split, and it is the construction the table cannot key: a preposition standing before a construct noun and rendered by a single English preposition. The chapter fuses it under rule 30 at 13.22 (LIPHNE -> before) and 13.24 (AL ODOT -> because of), and splits it where each morpheme holds English of its own, at 13.3 (AL PI -> according to / the commandment) and 13.29 (AL YAD -> along by / the side). But 13.32 rendered BETOKHAH as 'in it' by giving 'in' to the BE and marking TAVEKH unrepresented, which leaves a lexical noun holding no English while the one-rendering condition is met. Patched: BE + TAVEKH share one aligned unit on 'in', headed on TAVEKH, the suffix keeping 'it' as the nomen rectum under rule 19. Rule 19's own rider directs this, and rule 22 does not reach it, because TAVEKH is not a repetition of anything.

BSB: 18 comparable disagreements. Seventeen are the documented convention differences and none is an error — LE unrepresented under rules 27 and 40 (13.2 ethical dative, 13.16 bare object after 'called', 13.27 bare indirect object, 13.32 lemor), five object markers under rule 16, the resumptive HAH, HENNAH and HU under rule 22, articles with no written 'the' under rules 29 and 41, and the LA of the impersonal naming clause at 13.24 under rules 21 and 40. The eighteenth, TOKHAH at 13.32, is the genuine error above and is fixed here rather than to improve the rate. The 13.2 ISH and ECHAD flags are the doubled distributive under rule 22, whose competing reading the verse already names.

No promotion. The BETOKHAH correction is rule 19's rider and rule 30 applied, not a new rule; the positive existential YESH at 13.20 (taking 'there is' and heading on 'is', on rule 50's terms) is a single occurrence with no corpus precedent in this briefing, and a rule built on it would be paid for by every later chapter. Three conventions recorded instead.
